name: Silent Bell Strike
description: A single open-palm strike from the centre of the chest — the exact rhythm of the bronze bell at the Brother-Houses. The blow carries no qi and draws no sound. Its discipline is in the pause that precedes it: the strike is thrown between two beats of the opponent's breath, and is therefore never quite there.

name: Settling-Stone Sit
description: A half-meditation taken mid-fight: the feet root, the shoulders go loose, and the dantian is permitted, for one slow breath, to re-find its own level. An elder's art, not a duellist's. The body recovers what the moment can spare.

name: Viper-Sting Jab
description: The mortal-tier introduction to the Five Poisons' serpent work — a finger-jab to a meridian gap tipped with a palm-prepared tincture. Gatekeeper Wuwei teaches it only once, and only if the scorpion on his collar has not yet woken. The venom is small. The lesson is not.

name: Iron-Ox Shrug
description: A brawler's art taught in blacksmith yards and harvest-festival wrestling rings: the shoulders roll, the diaphragm locks, and the body gathers itself around a single forthcoming strike. What used to be a swing becomes a sweep. Forge-Master Bo names it without ceremony and teaches it without patience.

name: Azure Cloud Sword-Arc
description: The second form taught at the Sword Hall: a wide cutting arc with the hip driving the shoulder, the shoulder driving the wrist, and the wrist giving way to a curl of blue qi at the point. Delivered honestly, the arc is both strike and a preparation for the next strike. Its teaching verse is the eighteen words Baixu will not let his disciples paraphrase.

name: Crane-Wing Parry
description: A single arrested sweep of the blade, reading the incoming stroke and turning it off the vertical. The wrist does almost nothing; the shoulder does everything. Baixu's disciples are taught it before the Azure Cloud Sword; he will not explain why.

name: Flashing Willow-Leaf
description: A cut so light it almost does not trouble the cloth before it troubles the flesh. Meilin names it 'the thing Baixu does not like me teaching', because the wound opens honestly and then does not stop. The technique is best against a foe in heavy robes; the cloth hides the cut for a round, then ruins them.

name: Black-Lattice Palm
description: An outer-palm strike of the Black Lattice, Apothecary Qi's private work. No poison — only a lattice of faintly dark qi woven across the skin where it lands, which parts the meridian wall on impact and does not re-knit. The wound bleeds as though it remembered a previous wound to complete.

name: Mountain-Root Stance
description: A smith's stance, taken from the manner of standing in front of a four-hundred-pound hammer when it is about to fall. The heel digs; the dantian settles under the navel; the shoulders loosen so the blow need not travel through a tense back to find its answer. For the next three breaths, a struck body is half a mountain.

name: Crimson Hand of Silence
description: A short close-range palm the Pavilion's elders teach only after the second oath. The hand meets the sternum with a flat report; the blow rings up the spine and shakes loose the word the victim was about to speak. For one beat of the heart, the voice does not obey. Elder Red Feather says this is the oldest service a red sleeve can offer a friend.

name: Nine-Cloud Cranes' Flight
description: The sword-form no Azure disciple is permitted to learn without first spending a winter at the Library. Nine flowing cuts, each suggesting the shape of a crane ascending; what looks like nine separate strikes is, from the correct angle, a single cut which the world happens to witness from nine places. Elder Baixu calls it 'the form I taught my first student and did not see again for twenty years.'

name: Five-Venoms Brocade Palm
description: Matriarch Shan's own refinement of the Five Poisons Palm. Five venoms are layered through the palm as the colours of a brocade: one poisons, one slows, one paralyses, one brings sleep, and the fifth is only the dye that holds the others in pattern. The victim is poisoned, and then, more interestingly, continues to be poisoned in ways the first breath did not promise.

name: Heart-Boiling Technique
description: The Pavilion's foundation-tier expansion of the Blood Lotus Palm. Where the lotus draws a petal of qi, the boiling draws a cup. The striker receives, back across the wound, a hot draught of the victim's own life; the victim, in the same moment, remembers their mother's kitchen for no reason they can name. Elder Red Feather warns against it for anyone who has known grief recently.

name: Stormwarden's Mantle
description: A Sky-Spire discipline, learned by the wardens who walk the ridge in weather. The practitioner draws a thin mantle of storm-qi around the shoulders; for three breaths, the body moves as though the air around it were pushing with the swing, not against it. It is the single technique Stormwarden Gao will teach only to those who have survived the ridge in her company.

name: Brass-Bell Sutra
description: Huilin's own work, named for the iron staff that carries the bell he will not ring. The sutra is a slow three-note breath set against an opponent's pulse; each note closes a wound the previous note re-opened, and by the third the body has forgotten it was cut. Useless in a rout; kinder than a pill in a hard fight.
